# Sorcerer

> Sorcerer is a free, open-source (MIT), native macOS app that simulates small communities of AI agents around a "what if…?" question. You summon characters with personalities, goals, relationships and memory, drop in a hypothesis, and watch opinions form, collide and spread round by round. It is local-first and runs on CLI sessions (Claude Code, Codex or Gemini), Ollama, LM Studio or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It is made for curiosity and fun, not forecasting.

- Platform: macOS 15 or later, Apple silicon and Intel (universal app), built with SwiftUI, no dependencies
- Price: free; no Sorcerer account or server; API keys optional, remote API usage may be billed
- Data: everything is stored as plain JSON in ~/Sorcerer on your Mac
- Inspired by MiroFish; a separate, from-scratch implementation

## Features

- Scheduled events: choose a future round; edit or remove pending events while paused; plans persist per branch
- Saved 1:1 chats: transcripts persist locally per experiment and branch and are excluded from share exports
- CSV cast import: UTF-8 CSV, 2–16 characters, local validation and preview before starting; no AI call to import
- Experiments: write a what-if question, pick a setting (social feed, forum, group chat, town square, workplace), rounds and speed
- Context brief: point it at a GitHub repo, folder, website or files; facts are tagged public, insider or hidden so each character only knows what they would know. Secrets like .env files are never read
- Live rounds: characters post, reply to specific posts, react, remember, and are influenced by their ties; text streams in as it is written
- Views: feed, world map of relationships, mood graph per character
- Characters: profiles, 1:1 chat off the record or in-world, persona editing, pixel-art avatar editor
- Branches: fork the world and compare futures; reports with a sentiment chart and findings that cite the exact posts
- Usage limits: reads your Claude 5-hour and weekly windows and pauses before you hit them
- Export experiments with full history or as a fresh scenario; anyone can read an exported .sorcerer.json in the browser at https://sorcererapp.dev/view without installing the app
